_comment: GH#43 parser-conformance sweep. Each case pins a CITED or MEASURED string from the sweep of the vendored models.dev catalog against the production parser, and the entity key the production path produces for it TODAY. 'key' is the MEASURED key, so the corpus is a witness of current behaviour and goes red when any of these keys moves. 'conformance' says whether that key is right: 'conforming' (the key is correct, the cited defect is refuted at this tip), 'defect' (the key is wrong and 'want_key' states the correct destination), or 'undecided' (the destination is a curation ruling this sweep must not invent, and 'want_key' is the EXPECTED_TBD marker). The sweep CHANGES NO KEY: it only records.

provenance.ref: GH#43 defect class 2, measured at this tip: the lab-side (metadata) decomposition of this id makes the WHOLE id the family. It DISAGREES with the serving-side key nemotron/v1.5@3.3#49b for the identical id, and the served sibling case pins that other key, so the disagreement itself is the falsifiable fact. Which key both paths must agree ON is a curation ruling the sweep does not invent: the served key states the version v1.5 in the variant slot, which is the class 1 defect, so it is not automatically the right destination either.

mutation.description: the lab-id path has no upstream raw family to lean on; the id-only decomposition then takes the entire id as the family

provenance.ref: GH#43 defect class 2, measured at this tip: the SERVED side of the identical id keys nemotron/v1.5@3.3#49b, while the lab side keys llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b/v1.5@3.3#49b. This case is the second half of the disagreement pair: with both keys pinned, the disagreement is falsifiable, and it goes green only when the two paths agree. The destination is a curation ruling, so the case carries EXPECTED_TBD, as classes 4 and 5 do.

mutation.description: the served path reads the upstream raw family beside the id, so it reduces the compound name where the id-only lab path cannot

provenance.ref: Flash-variant uniformity (UAT ruling, GH#43 follow-up): 'flash' is a distinct-weight VARIANT, and the trailing 'v' on GLM is the VISION modality. The id keys glm/v@4.1{flash} today: 'v' is read as the variant and 'flash' as an identity modifier, the exact inversion of the ruling, and the 'thinking' token is dropped. The correct destination is glm/flash@4.1{vision}.

mutation.description: the flash variant and the vision 'v' both land in the wrong slot: 'v' becomes the variant and 'flash' a modifier, and 'thinking' is dropped

The fully-correct final key also drops the {z} prefix artifact, reads the vision 'v' as the {vision} modifier (UAT vision ruling), and leaves turbo off the key: glm@5{vision}.

mutation.description: the same z-ai prefix on a glm-5v id; the leftover 'z' lands in the modifier slot, and the vision 'v' is read as the variant, so the final correct key must fix both

provenance.ref: GH#43 defect class 3: the SAME model under a SLASH-separated namespace strips the prefix correctly, so no {z} modifier leaks (contrast the dash-glued z-ai case above, which keys glm/v@5{z}). But even with the prefix stripped the vision 'v' is still read as the variant, so the key glm/v@5 remains a defect under the UAT vision ruling; the fully-correct final key is glm@5{vision}. This isolates the prefix cause AND shows the residual vision defect survives correct stripping.

mutation.description: replaces the dash-glued z-ai prefix with a slash-separated zai namespace; the prefix is stripped correctly, but the vision 'v' defect remains

mutation.description: the same turbo token on a v3 id; with turbo off the key the collision splits by the real base and the v3 version is restored

provenance.ref: GH#43 defect class 4, resolved by UAT ruling: Claude Code is a harness/agent, not model weights (Poe passthrough, 0 context / 0 cost), so it does not belong in the keyspace at all. The id keys claude{code} today, reading the product name as an identity modifier on the claude family; the ruling EXCLUDES it. The pinned key is the witness that today's parser still produces a key, so the exclusion goes red if that stops being true.

mutation.description: a product/harness name on a claude id; the ruling removes it from the keyspace rather than assigning it a want-key
